fieldValues.title: A squash/history rewrite on master orphans commit-pinned allowlist entries
fieldValues.summary: scripts/versioning-cell-allowlist.json's disposition schema pins a violation by commit SHA (fromCommit/toCommit). Master's history was rewritten (force-pushed) after the pinned commits were made: one commit no longer exists as a git object at all, and the other is no longer an ancestor of origin/master, even though its tree content is present in the live corpus. The check that reads those pins (check-versioning-cell.mjs) can then no longer observe the transition at all, and reports the entry as 'no longer matches a violation' — a false negative for the mechanism, not a fixed corpus.
evidence: git cat-file -t 3553f2ac -> fatal: Not a valid object name (the commit does not exist anywhere in the repository)
git merge-base --is-ancestor 72c5d2b7 origin/master -> false, despite 72c5d2b7 existing as a real, reachable-from-some-ref commit object with the exact tree diff the allowlist entry describes
A stale local master ref predating this session's `git fetch` (74c39e8) DOES contain 72c5d2b7 as an ancestor, and the fetch itself reported 'forced update' -- direct evidence of the rewrite

On current master, srs/package/metamodel/fields/value_range.json first appears as a `new file mode` diff (not an edit) in an unrelated commit (679dc13, 'retire the v1 epic protocol files'), meaning the incremental history that would let the check re-derive the transition is gone, not just the exact SHA pins

Fixed in srs#668/PR #669 by emptying the allowlist's entries array, matching the check's own documented remedy ('shrinking this file IS the fix'); verified this restores validate-all.mjs and check-release-drift.mjs to green
fieldValues.body: Any allowlist or exclusion-list schema that pins a historical transition by commit SHA (rather than by content, path, or a stable id) is fragile against a rewritten base branch -- and this repository's own branch-cleanup and force-push activity (see srs#580's Wave 1) makes that a live risk, not a hypothetical one. versioning-cell-allowlist.json is currently the ONLY allowlist in scripts/*.json using commit pins (grep for fromCommit/toCommit); its siblings (spec-coherence-allowlist.json, publication-reachability-exclusions.json, repository-cell-allowlist.json) key by path/instanceId/reason instead and are immune to this failure mode. If a future check adopts a similar commit-pinned shape, expect the same class of break after any history rewrite, and the same remedy: the pin cannot be repaired (the intervening history is gone), only removed, and the underlying issue it was tracking (if still real) needs its own re-verification against the live corpus rather than the git-log diff the check used to rely on.
